paragraphs: Public libraries in mid-sized cities have been written off repeatedly as relics of the print era, yet usage figures tell a more complicated story. Book lending has indeed declined in most branches. Some critics take this as proof that libraries have outlived their purpose. But the same branches report steady growth in attendance, driven by job-search workshops, language classes, and free access to computers and quiet rooms. It seems likely that libraries will survive not by lending more books but by serving as one of the few remaining public spaces that charge nothing for entry, although whether municipal budgets will adapt to this change is far from certain.
